The strongest positives are IMF-backed corrective reforms, not proof of success.\n\nThe best negative evidence is broader and more convincing: inflation, reserve pressure, currency weakness, and high-risk capital spending all remained serious problems.","evidence":[{"title":"Bangladesh: Second Reviews Under the ECF/EFF and RSF Arrangements","publisher":"IMF","date":"June 24, 2024","url":"https://www.elibrary.imf.org/view/journals/002/2024/186/article-A001-en.xml","summary":"The IMF said Bangladesh’s program performance was broadly on track and that the authorities had realigned the exchange rate, adopted a crawling peg, tightened monetary policy, and pursued tax/subsidy reforms to safeguard macro stability.
